chunks: Rijal al-Kashshi: Muhammad b. Qulawayh and al-Husayn b. al-Hasan b. Bundar al-Qummi, from Sa'd b. Abdallah b. Abi Khalaf al-Qummi, from al-Hasan b. Musa al-Khashshab and Muhammad b. Isa b. Ubid, from Ali b. Asbat, from Abdallah b. Sinan who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying:
Muhammad b. Abi Bakr - May Allah’s mercy be upon him - his noble descent (nisabah) was from his mother Asma bt. Umays

key_terms.أَسْمَاءُ بِنْتُ عُمَيْسٍ: Asma bint Umays, a prominent companion of the Prophet

ai.seo_question: Who was the mother of Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr according to Shia hadith sources?
ai.summary: This narration from Rijal al-Kashshi underscores the significance of Asma bint Umys in Shia genealogical records, where Muhammad b. Abi Bakr’s lineage is traced through her, reflecting the prominence of maternal lines in early Islamic history. Asma, a close companion of the Prophet and later of Imam Ali (AS), played a key role in transmitting knowledge and maintaining the legacy of the Ahl al-Bayt, making this detail both historically and theologically significant.
